source.unit: parallel parent keeps own bound map

natural_facts: 117 creates a fresh child with depth one greater and copies the current parent event number.
Its setup supplies no map argument, so setup binds the child to the then-current map. The parent map binding is not assigned by this call.
The child runs before further parent commands. Private variables/default self-switches/event-time helpers consume each interpreter own map binding.
Connected-map context preserves the parent event number, allowing parent(A,7), child(B,7), and current target(B,7) to differ.

dual_evidence.production_consumer_chain: A-map parallel event sets parent(A,7) -> current map remains B ->117 creates child(B,7)->child private write uses [B,7] -> child ends -> parent private write uses [A,7]. Private store is global_metadata save value; physical save/reload not executed.

finite_domain: Valid resident connected maps A≠B, current map B and no transfer during observation.
A/7 parallel parent was started with explicit A binding, remains running and receives an update; event id7 remains due to connectivity.
A valid common event record at positive ID K has a legal script command writing one private value and a terminator.
All normal helper/dispatch dependencies return, no waiting, plugin override, extra write or index-changing helper.
premises_and_counterexamples.ordinary_control: With current map A equal parent binding, child and parent private writes both use[A,7].

steps: Start parent(A,7), keep B current and connected.
Parent executes117(K); child writes marker child through one-argument private setter and ends.
Parent writes marker parent through one-argument private setter and ends.
minimal_counterexample.expected: [B,7]=child, [A,7]=parent. Child does not write[A,7]; parent original binding remains A.
minimal_counterexample.current_spec_difference: Current generic identity paragraphs do not explicitly state what117 propagates and rebinds. Candidate is a coverage clarification, not an alleged false claim that child inherits A.

premises_and_counterexamples.cancel: 117 has no cancellation interface; an absent record skips child creation and normal outer advancement continues.
premises_and_counterexamples.failure: Depth101/child script/setup failures stop at actual prefix; child private writes already completed are not rolled back; no host recovery guarantee.
premises_and_counterexamples.partial_commit: A successful child private write remains when a later child/parent operation fails; parent retained binding unchanged by the setup call.
premises_and_counterexamples.disconnected_control: If parent map becomes disconnected, update clears its event number to0 before117; child binds[B,0], not this[A/B,7] example.
